context: Therefore in any optimal labeling, at least one port is in S. Since the order is fixed, choosing a specific label to have its port at an element in S fixes all other ports and specifically the location of the port of pmin . Therefore every element of S induces n possible choices for this port which results in n2 choices in total. ◀ In general, the previous method does not extend to the problems in OR-C O SA, since choosing one element in S still leaves (n−1)! possible orders of the remaining labels. However, in the special case where both the label sizes and the port ratios are uniform, we know that all ports in any valid labeling are distributed equally along B, which implies that again every element in S induces exactly n possible labels (even if we do not know which label is connected to which port).
